question: If the distance between the centres of two circles is 12 cm and the radii are 5 cm and 4 cm, then the length (in cm) of the transverse common tangent is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The length of the **transverse common tangent (TCT)** is calculated using the direct formula:

**TCT** = √[d² − (r₁ + r₂)²]

Where **d** is the distance between centres, and **r₁, r₂** are the radii.

⇒ TCT = √[12² − (5 + 4)²]

⇒ TCT = √[144 − 81] = √63

**∴ The correct answer is √63 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between centres (**d**) = 12 cm

Radius of first circle (**R**) = 5 cm

Radius of second circle (**r**) = 4 cm

**Formula Used:**

Length of **Transverse Common Tangent** = √[(Distance between centres)² − (Sum of radii)²]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f4e458fb3cc30948ea1eabc0c64550e0f8a38317f85c52a5ce828820c546ff3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of radii = R + r = 5 + 4 = 9 cm

⇒ Length of TCT = √[12² − (9)²]

⇒ Length of TCT = √[144 − 81]

⇒ Length of TCT = √63 cm

**∴ The correct answer is √63 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

The length of the direct common tangent is given by the formula: DCT = √[d² − (R − r)²].

Existence of Tangents

A transverse common tangent exists only if the distance between the centres is greater than or equal to the sum of the radii (d ≥ R + r).

Common Tangent Cases

If two circles touch each other externally, d = R + r, and there are 3 common tangents (2 direct and 1 transverse).</p
